answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents deposit POA into a shared on-chain anchor that scales the required stake with the square root of active identities, while each must complete peer verification tasks that form a mutual jetty of countersignatures. Only after three independent attestations can an agent access the transfer oasis where balances move. An attacker creating many identities faces linearly growing locked capital plus repeated computation for each jetty slot, exceeding expected mining yield once the network exceeds a few thousand participants.
